question: How many Falcon 9 or Falcon Heavy orbital launches will SpaceX have in the second half of November 2026?

calls.reasoning: Reference class: recent half-month Falcon counts in a declining-cadence regime (Oct 1-15 ~5, Oct 16-31 5, Nov 1-12 already 5). October 2026 had 10 orbital launches; trailing-365 rate fell below 150 (~6/15d) and is declining as SpaceX winds down Falcon for Starship. Window manifest: USSF-317 and USSF-266 (Nov 18, both Vandenberg, one likely slips), NROL-136 (Nov 21), NG-25 (Nov 29), plus undated Starlink 15-21, OneWeb 21, NROL-195 and unannounced Starlinks. Expected count ~5 with modest dispersion; 5-6 slightly favored over 3-4. No matching human market found (Manifold candidates are unrelated contracts).

calls.reconciliation: Main factual dispute: how many launches in Nov 1-12 (Run 1 said 5; Runs 2-3 said 3). Spacenexus lists 2 flown (USSF-432 Nov 7, USSF-627 Nov 12) and omits SDA T1; NextSpaceflight lists USSF-432 and USSF-627 and shows USSF-317 launching Nov 13 04:23 UTC. I could not confirm Run 1's Nov 2 and Nov 5 Starlink launches, so I favor the lower ~3-4 count. Second check: USSF-317 is pre-window per NextSpaceflight, while spacenexus still lists it Nov 18 alongside USSF-266 (two same-day launches from one Vandenberg pad are implausible). So the window loses one listed candidate. Wikipedia fetch was truncated (the 2026 table did not come through); its header says 716 Falcon-family launches as of Nov 12. Florida: no Falcon Starlink in November confirmed; NG-25 is the only listed Florida Falcon flight. Judgment: Vandenberg turnaround caps the count near 4-5. Weighted toward Runs 2-3 but kept substantial mass on 5-6.

disagreements.verdict: Trackers show ~3 (USSF-432, SDA T1, USSF-627); Run 1's extra Starlinks unconfirmed. Favor 3.
NextSpaceflight shows it launching Nov 13 UTC, before the window; other trackers stale.
Evidence supports ~4-4.5 given Vandenberg-only cadence plus NG-25.
Likely but slip risk; counted at ~65-70%.
